request:
Stop preemptively rejecting fork and permission cases

## Problem

GitWeave currently performs preemptive repository/permission checks before some existing-PR mutations.

In particular, it rejects cross-repository PR heads up front and checks repository `permissions.push` before attempting mutation.

This can block workflows that GitHub itself may allow. A clear example is merging a clean fork Pull Request: merging does not require pushing to the fork head branch, yet GitWeave's current writable check can reject the operation before GitHub evaluates the merge request.

These checks encode anticipated permission policy inside GitWeave instead of letting the actual Git/GitHub operation determine whether it is allowed.

## Expected outcome

Remove preemptive repository/permission rejection where the underlying operation can determine success or failure directly.

Conceptually:

```text
sync_pr
  → attempt the exact intended branch update
  → Git/GitHub accepts or rejects it

merge_pr
  → request the exact merge
  → GitHub accepts or rejects it
```

Do not reject a fork PR merely because its head repository differs from the base repository.

Do not require an additional GitHub `permissions.push` preflight check when the actual push or merge operation is already authoritative.

Keep only checks that are required to identify the correct target and avoid writing to the wrong ref.

Surface the real Git/GitHub failure if the operation is not permitted.

## Context

The guiding principle is:

> Do not predict whether an operation might be disallowed when Git or GitHub can authoritatively answer that by performing the requested operation.

If a concrete incorrect-target or destructive-write problem is observed later, address that specific problem separately.


User directive: GitWeave implements, creates a separate PR, reviews/fixes iteratively and merges only when clean. Stop on unsupported operations or permission/allowance limits and ask the user. No parent manual substitute is authorized.
